minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to suspend grease trap fees another year, add a part-timer, and move money into capital.
minutes.summary: Budget workshop walking through the FY22 sewer enterprise budget line by line. The commission voted to suspend grease trap fees for FY22, approved a 19-hour part-time position without benefits (one member against), and agreed to put a large sum from retained earnings into the infrastructure/capital line. Fitchburg and Leominster cost estimates were raised, and a regular automatic rate increase was floated for the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to suspend grease trap permit fees for fiscal 2022.
The commission approved a 19-hour-a-week part-time position with no benefits; one member voted no.
The commission voted, on a roll call, to move a sum from retained earnings into the capital and infrastructure line.
The revised budget will raise the engineering services subline and the Leominster and Fitchburg usage estimates.
The budget is to be finalized and submitted at the next meeting; a regular automatic rate increase was left for later discussion.

why_it_matters: Sewer costs are paid by users through their bills, so the fee waiver, the new position and the use of retained earnings affect what the sewer enterprise collects and holds, not the general tax levy.
The reserve capacity fund that covers the Fitchburg payment is being drawn down, so a later rate increase, the one floated for a future meeting, may be needed to replace it.
watch_next: The next meeting, where the revised FY22 sewer budget is to be finalized and submitted.
The proposed regular automatic rate increase, set for later discussion.
